visual_evidence_readiness.summary: Numerical visual parity EN/PT-BR, units and period labels, source-linked tables, geographic mechanism and causal flow.
visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 3 evidence tables + 3 charts + 1 flow + 1 map each locale

research_depth.summary: Fed/ECB policy divergence, Eurostat energy inflation, BLS September employment, IBGE IPCA, global debt and financial-stability transmission, four falsifiable scenarios.

evidence_traceability.summary: Official primary releases: Fed September 16, ECB September 10, Eurostat October 2 flash, BLS October 2, IBGE October 9, IMF fiscal and GFSR April; forthcoming events not presented as outcomes.

counterfactual_review.summary: Energy easing, persistent imported inflation, nonbank funding repricing and productivity improvements are competing conditional paths with discriminating evidence.

contrary_evidence: September Eurostat flash does not alone invalidate September ECB full-year projections.
Lower energy import prices would moderate pressure even without a rate cut.
Higher long-bond yields can result from productivity or term premiums as well as fiscal risk.
Asia AI labour-market questions are not observations of China-specific employment.
limitations: Historical, estimated, projected and scheduled observations labelled separately.
IMF global debt-at-risk is a conditional tail quantile, not a forecast average.
Inflation component rates and survey series are not automatically additive.
China-specific macro observations not manufactured from an Asian research agenda.
notes: Substantive revision 1 supersedes shallow edition. First-party numbers and visual EN/PT parity checked; successful staging CI 38207542797. No external independent peer-review claim.
